payload.description:
## Trigger

When a team on an existing tracker installs this kit into a repository that already holds a backlog, I want one command that imports their export, so I can move across without retyping every record and without the published README promising something that does not exist.

packages/basicly-tracker/README.md line 22 states 'It also imports a beads JSONL export, so a repository can move its backlog across without retyping it.' That is false. The installer never touches migrate: a grep for migrate, import_, beads and issues.jsonl across kit_installer.py and the package entry point returns nothing, against a positive control that migrate.py holds 12 functions and is real code. migrate.py has no main, no argparse and no CLI verb, so the capability exists and is unreachable for the consumer it was written for.

This is the same defect class as basicly-zsq6xkz, one layer out. That retro gated a design document sentence naming a call the code does not make, and left a README sentence naming a capability the code does not expose.

The engine wrapper src/basicly/tracker_import.py adds rendering and a dry run, not safety - every refusal comes from migrate itself and is already in ImportReport.rejected. So exposing the kit verb loses no guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A standalone consumer with no basicly runs one kit command to import an export and sees what was imported, what diverged and what was refused.
- A dry run reports the same numbers by the same code path and writes nothing, rather than approximating them.
- The README says only what the shipped command does, checked by running it.
- A test imports an export into a fresh ledger through the consumer surface, with a dry run first that leaves the ledger byte-identical as the control.
payload.title: expose the ledger import so a repository leaving beads can actually onboard
